cases.name: ho-h-derm-skin-tone
cases.promptMarkdown: For a fairness audit I want to test whether dermatology image classifiers do worse on darker skin. I need skin images where every image (or patient) comes with a skin tone label, either Fitzpatrick type or Monk scale, as well as a diagnosis, and the darker types (V and VI) have to actually be represented rather than a handful. Clinical photos or dermoscopy are both fine, and it doesn't have to be skin cancer only. Which public datasets have that?

graders.name: 01-recall-fitzpatrick17k
graders.evidence:
Five public datasets meet all three criteria (skin tone label, diagnosis, non-trivial V/VI); most of the well-known skin datasets fail on the third. I counted the skin-tone distributions directly from the metadata files for Fitzpatrick17k, SCIN, DermaCon-IN and the ISIC Archive; the DDI and PASSION numbers are from their papers.

## Datasets that qualify

| Dataset | Images | Skin tone label | Type V / VI | Diagnosis | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DDI** (Stanford) | 656 clinical, 570 patients | Fitzpatrick, grouped I–II / III–IV / V–VI | 207 images in V–VI (48 malignant) | 78 diseases plus benign/malignant; all malignancies biopsy-confirmed | Stanford AIMI, research use agreement |
| **Fitzpatrick17k** | 16,577 clinical | Fitzpatrick I–VI, assigned from the image by non-dermatologist annotators | 1,533 / 635 | 114 conditions from atlas captions, not biopsy | GitHub CSV of image URLs |
| **DermaCon-IN** (South India) | 5,450 clinical, ~3,000 patients | Fitzpatrick and Monk | Fitzpatrick 1,285 / 136; Monk 7–9: 2,059 | 245 diagnoses, dermatologist-labelled | Harvard Dataverse, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 |
| **PASSION** (Madagascar, Guinea, Malawi, Tanzania) | 4,901 clinical, 1,653 patients | Fitzpatrick III–VI | 341 / 88 in the 20% test split, so roughly 1,700 / 440 overall (my extrapolation) | Eczema, fungal, scabies, other, plus an impetigo flag | passionderm.github.io, own licence |
| **SCIN** (Google) | 10,407 consumer photos, 5,033 cases | Self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick, and Monk from lay raters | Dermatologist-estimated 359 / 69 cases; self-reported 214 / 143; Monk 7–10 (US raters): 207 | Dermatologist differential diagnoses, weighted, not biopsy | GitHub and public Google Cloud bucket |

## How I would use them

- **DDI as the headline test set.** It is the only one built for this audit: light and dark groups are matched on diagnosis category, age and sex, and the labels are pathology-backed. It is small, so confidence intervals will be wide.
- **Fitzpatrick17k for breadth.** It has the most V/VI images, but both the skin type and diagnosis labels are noisy, and only 89 of the 114 conditions have any type VI examples. The atlas images may also overlap with the training data of the classifiers you are auditing.
- **DermaCon-IN and PASSION for real clinic populations.** Both skew to inflammatory and infectious disease rather than cancer, and neither has lighter types (I–II) for a within-dataset comparison.
- **SCIN if the classifier targets consumer phone photos or you want Monk labels.** Type VI is thin and half the cases have no self-reported Fitzpatrick type.

Disease mix differs by skin tone in all of these, so compare within diagnosis, or a tone gap will partly be a case-mix gap.

## Near misses

- **MSKCC Skin Tone Labeling Dataset (ISIC Archive):** 4,879 images from 64 patients, balanced across Fitzpatrick I–VI (813 type V, 750 type VI), with Monk and colorimeter readings. Every lesion is labelled benign, so it only supports a false-positive-rate comparison.
- **PAD-UFES-20:** has a Fitzpatrick field, but only 10 type V and 1 type VI images.
- **MRA-MIDAS:** biopsy-proven paired clinical and dermoscopic images with Fitzpatrick type, but only 16.8% of patients are type III or darker.
- **MILK10k:** 10,480 paired images with a six-level skin tone field (not Fitzpatrick). Its documentation says most patients sit in the middle of the scale; I did not get the per-level counts.
- **Other ISIC collections (including HAM10000):** no usable skin tone labels with V/VI. The MSKCC set and PAD-UFES-20 are the only two collections in the archive with any type V or VI label.

- [DDI paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2203.08807) and [project page](https://ddi-dataset.github.io)
- [SCIN repository](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin) and [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18545)
- [PASSION paper](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2411.04584) and [dataset site](https://passionderm.github.io/)
- [DermaCon-IN paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.06099) and [Harvard Dataverse record](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM)
- [MSKCC Skin Tone Labeling Dataset](https://api.isic-archive.com/collections/413/)
- [MRA-MIDAS dataset page](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/mra-midas-Multimodal-Image-Dataset-for-AI-based-Skin-Cancer)
- [MILK10k dataset page](https://api.isic-archive.com/doi/milk10k/)

graders.name: 01-recall-german-iab
graders.evidence:
There is one real dataset you can probably hold within days to weeks (Veneto Worker Histories), one that may be downloadable today (Chile's unemployment insurance sample), and a serious long-run option whose application you should start now (German IAB data). I checked the access pages for those three today; the "from memory" rows below are from my own knowledge and need checking before you rely on them.

## Options, ranked by how fast you could be working

| Data | What it is | What access takes | Fit for an AKM decomposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Veneto Worker Histories (Italy)** | Social security records, 1975–2001; all private-sector employees of firms in the covered area, with workers followed when they leave it | Sign a form and email it to Fondazione Rodolfo Debenedetti; the page lists no fee or eligibility test, and you get the files themselves | Good. A standard AKM dataset, but it ends in 2001 and covers one region |
| **Chile Seguro de Cesantía sample** | Public anonymised samples of 3%, 5% and 12% of affiliates, combinable to 20%, updated yearly | Download from the Superintendencia de Pensiones | Uncertain. A worker sample, and I could not confirm the employer ID (see below) |
| **Spain MCVL** | 4% sample of people in social security records, with full work histories and anonymised firm IDs (from memory) | Institutional application to Seguridad Social for non-commercial research; I found no nationality rule, but could not confirm that foreign institutions qualify | Moderate. A worker sample, with capped earnings unless you get the tax-data version |
| **Italy LoSaI** | Roughly 7% sample of private-sector workers, 1985–2016 | Research proposal to the Ministry of Labour, signed by you and your institution's data contact, plus confidentiality declarations | Moderate. Again a worker sample |
| **Germany IAB (SIEED, LIAB)** | SIEED: 1% of establishments with all their workers' full biographies, 1975–2023 | Project application and a contract with your institution; no scientific use file, so on-site or remote execution only | Very good. Establishments rather than firms, and wages are top-coded |
| **Portugal Quadros de Pessoal** | Annual census of private-sector firms and their workers, uncapped wages (from memory) | Accreditation through Statistics Portugal or the Banco de Portugal microdata lab | Excellent if you can get in; easiest with a Portuguese coauthor |
| **France DADS panel** | Long worker panel from payroll declarations (from memory) | Confidentiality committee approval, then a paid secure-access device from CASD; expect months | Good, but a worker sample |
| **US LEHD** | Near-universe state unemployment insurance records | Census research data centre proposal, security clearance, usually a year or more; hard for non-US nationals (from memory) | Excellent, but not a second-year starting point |
| **Nordic registers, Netherlands** | Full population registers | Usually a local institutional affiliation or host, plus fees (from memory) | Excellent with a local coauthor |
| **Brazil RAIS** | Universe of formal jobs | The identified version needs a ministry agreement or an insider coauthor (from memory) | Excellent, but the public version has no worker IDs, so it is useless for AKM |

- **IAB from outside Germany:** remote desktop is limited to institutions based in Germany. Remote job submission (JoSuA) is the fallback, and it is slow because you only see vetted output.
- **IAB shortcuts:** test data for SIEED is downloadable so you can write code before approval. The IAB also publishes pre-estimated AKM person and establishment effects (1985–2023) that merge into its datasets.

3. **If you need recent years quickly:** check the Chilean codebook for the employer ID, and apply for MCVL or LoSaI depending on where your institution sits.

Veneto alone will not answer a question about the recent rise in inequality, since it stops in 2001. Tell me where your institution is and I can narrow the list, because eligibility for most of these runs through the institution.

graders.evidence:
**Short answer:** the only data you can realistically be working with within days to weeks is the Veneto Worker History (VWH) file from Italy. The best data you can get on a PhD timeline is the German IAB data, which takes a few months. I checked the VWH and IAB access pages today; everything else below is from memory and should be confirmed with the provider.

## Start right away

**Veneto Worker History (Italy, 1975–2001)**
- **What it is:** matched worker-firm panel built from social security records, with every worker followed across their whole career. It is the dataset used in Card, Devicienti and Maida (2014) and in Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten (2020), so replication code exists.
- **Access:** sign a one-page form and email it to the Fondazione Rodolfo Debenedetti (info@frdb.org). The page lists no fee and no eligibility conditions.
- **Limits:** one region, the series ends in 2001, and earnings are annual with no hours. The distributor's page describes coverage as Treviso and Vicenza provinces, while papers using it describe all of Veneto, so ask which version you are getting.

**IAB test data (Germany)**
- The IAB's research data centre lets you write and debug code against artificial test data before you have real access.
- This is only for building the pipeline; the numbers are meaningless.

## Feasible in months

| Data | What it takes | Catch |
|---|---|---|
| **Germany: SIAB / LIAB** (1975 onward) | Your supervisor's chair must submit the request, as a Word form. Review takes up to a month, then your institution signs a use agreement. You then submit code for remote execution or work on-site. I recall no fee. | Earnings are top-coded and need imputation. From outside the EU, use remote execution: on-site use in the US, Canada or UK needs a stay of nine months or more and extra anonymisation. |
| **Spain: MCVL** (4% sample, 2004 onward plus retrospective histories) | Institutional request form to Social Security. Free, and I recall turnaround in weeks. | The sample is small for AKM. I could not confirm whether institutions outside Spain qualify. |
| **Italy: LoSaI** (roughly 6.5% sample, 1985 onward) | Project-based request to the Ministry of Labour. | I could not confirm the current procedure or the firm identifier; check before counting on it. |
| **France: DADS panel / Base Tous Salariés** | Approval by the statistical secrecy committee, then a paid secure-access box through CASD. Expect several months and a few thousand euros a year. | The long panel is a sample of roughly 1 in 12; the full file does not link workers across years directly. |

## A year or more, or needs an insider

- **US LEHD:** proposal through a Federal Statistical Research Data Center, with Census and state approvals and Special Sworn Status. Expect a year or more, and non-citizens face a residency requirement. This is realistic only if your university has a centre and a faculty member already has a project.

- **Italy, INPS universe:** through the competitive VisitINPS programme, on site in Rome.

graders.name: 01-recall-galaxy-zoo-2
graders.evidence:
**Download Galaxy Zoo 2 (GZ2) as your main dataset.** It meets every requirement: about 191k SDSS galaxies in the bundled version, labels that are purely volunteer votes, and images packaged with the labels.

I checked the sources below online today but did not download anything.

## Primary: Galaxy Zoo 2

- **Hugging Face `mwalmsley/gz2`** is the easiest route: about 191k galaxies (172k train / 18.8k test) as 424×424 images with per-question vote counts and fractions in the same parquet files. It should load with `datasets.load_dataset("mwalmsley/gz2")`, though I did not run this. The licence is CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0, which is fine for a thesis.
- **Labels:** the GZ2 decision tree covers smooth/featured, edge-on, bar, spiral arms (winding and arm count), bulge prominence, roundedness, and "odd features" (ring, lens, disturbed, irregular, merger, dust lane). The Hugging Face page preview was truncated, so I only saw the first few columns; the rest is from my knowledge of GZ2.
- **Manual alternative:** images from [Zenodo 3565489](https://zenodo.org/records/3565489) (243,434 JPGs, 3.4 GB, CC-BY 4.0, with a filename-mapping CSV) plus the Hart et al. (2016) vote table from [data.galaxyzoo.org](https://data.galaxyzoo.org/) (239,695 galaxies). That table is the one the Galaxy Zoo team recommends.

## If you want deeper images: Galaxy Zoo DECaLS

DECaLS imaging shows faint bars, arms and tidal features better than SDSS, and it has a dedicated merger question (none / minor disturbance / major disturbance / merger).

- **[Zenodo 4573248](https://zenodo.org/records/4573248)** (CC-BY 4.0) has the PNG images in four zips totalling about 104 GB, plus the volunteer tables.
- **Use only** `gz_decals_volunteers_5.parquet` (GZD-5, about 230k galaxies) and optionally `gz_decals_volunteers_1_and_2.parquet`.
- **Do not use** `gz_decals_auto_posteriors.*` in the same record: those are CNN predictions, which you have ruled out.
- **Easier download:** `pip install galaxy-datasets`, then `from galaxy_datasets import gz_decals_5` with `download=True` fetches images and the volunteer catalogue together. The same package also offers `gz2`, `gz_hubble` and `gz_candels`.

## What to avoid

- **Galaxy Zoo DESI (8.7M galaxies):** the headline catalogue is model predictions.
- **Galaxy10 DECaLS:** human-labelled but only about 18k galaxies and 10 coarse classes (figure from memory).

## Practical points for the thesis

- **Vote counts vary.** Questions deeper in the tree (bar, arm count) are only answered by volunteers who said "featured, not edge-on", so filter on the number of votes for each question before trusting a fraction.
- **Raw versus debiased.** The Hart table gives both raw and redshift-debiased fractions. Train on the raw ones, since they describe what is visible in the image; the debiased ones are for population statistics.
- **Loss function.** The standard approach is to predict vote counts with a Dirichlet-multinomial loss (Walmsley et al. 2022, the `zoobot` package), which handles the varying vote counts properly.

graders.name: 01-recall-galaxy-zoo-2
graders.evidence:
**Download Galaxy Zoo DESI from Hugging Face (`mwalmsley/gz_desi`).** It meets every requirement: about 399k galaxies, images bundled with the labels, and the labels are raw volunteer vote counts per answer.

I checked the dataset listings and cards online today, but did not download or open the image files themselves.

| Dataset | Galaxies | Size | Labels |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mwalmsley/gz_desi` | 399,413 | ~17.5 GB | bar (none/weak/strong), spiral arms, bulge size (5 levels), merging (none/minor disturbance/major disturbance/merger), plus edge-on, arm count and winding |
| `mwalmsley/gz2` | 191,174 (172,377 train / 18,797 test) | ~2.6 GB | bar, spiral arms, arm count, winding, bulge size, roundedness, "something odd" — no merger column |

Pick `gz_desi` if mergers matter. If you want something lighter and can live without merger labels, `gz2` is the classic SDSS benchmark and a seventh of the download.

```python
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("mwalmsley/gz_desi", split="train")   # name="tiny" for a 1% subset to prototype
```

Both are ungated and free, with a fixed train/test split.

Things to know before you commit:

- **Licence:** CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0, and the curator additionally requires that models trained on the data be released as source code by publication. That is fine for a thesis, but you will need to publish your code.
- **Vote counts vary by question:** volunteers answer a decision tree, so "bar?" is only asked of those who said "featured, not edge-on". Filter on the `*_total-votes` columns or use a vote-count-aware loss rather than a plain argmax.
- **Three campaigns in DESI:** the columns are suffixed `dr12`, `dr5` and `dr8`, with slightly different answer sets (for example, bar is yes/no in `dr12` but none/weak/strong in `dr5` and `dr8`). Each galaxy only has votes from its own campaign; `dr5` and `dr8` have the richer schema.
- **Avoid lookalikes:** the Galaxy Zoo DESI and DECaLS catalogues on Zenodo also ship model-predicted morphologies for millions of galaxies, which would break your human-labels rule. The Hugging Face columns above are volunteer counts according to the dataset card.

Two others I ruled out: Galaxy10 DECaLS is only about 17.7k images with 10 coarse classes (figure from memory), and `mwalmsley/gz_evo` (806k galaxies, 540 label columns across five campaigns and telescopes) is more than a master's CNN needs.
